One of ClickHouse's integration tests checks that a node correctly cleans up incomplete snapshot transfers to remote object storage after restarting.

*   In tests/integration/test_keeper_snapshot_chunked_transfer/test.py, in the test_recover_after_interrupted_transfer function, replace the set that records interrupted-transfer temporary objects using only the object name with a set that records each object as a tuple of its name and last-modification timestamp, so that each recorded entry uniquely identifies a specific object written at a specific point in time.

*   In tests/integration/test_keeper_snapshot_chunked_transfer/test.py, in the same function's polling loop, update the filter condition that checks for lingering interrupted-transfer objects to match against the tuple of object name and last-modification timestamp rather than against the object name alone, so that a new in-flight object with a coincidentally matching name is not mistaken for the original interrupted-transfer object.


*   Interface details: Type: File
Name: test.py
Location: tests/integration/test_keeper_snapshot_chunked_transfer/test.py
Description: Python integration test file for ClickHouse's keeper snapshot chunked transfer feature. The function test_recover_after_interrupted_transfer must be modified in the remote-storage code path. Specifically, the set that records which temporary bucket objects were left behind by the interrupted transfer must be changed to store (object_name, last_modified) tuples instead of object names alone. The polling loop within the same function that waits for those objects to be cleaned up must also be updated to filter objects using the same tuple-based comparison, so that a newly created object with the same name but a different modification timestamp is excluded from the match. The parametrized test variants that exercise the remote-disk path rely on this function.

Author: Groene AI <270696204+groeneai@users.noreply.github.com>
Date:   Thu Apr 16 16:28:47 2026 +0000

    Fix flaky test_keeper_snapshot_chunked_transfer by narrowing S3 tmp assertion
    
    The test_recover_after_interrupted_transfer[remote_disk] test was flaky
    because it asserted that *all* tmp_snapshot_* files are absent from S3
    immediately after restart + sync.  After restart, Keeper may create
    new local snapshots asynchronously (queued via snapshots_queue), which
    temporarily produce fresh tmp_ markers during serializeSnapshotToDisk.
    The immediate assertion catches these transient markers as false positives.
    
    The local_disk variant was never flaky because it checks the specific
    tmp file path from the interrupted transfer, ignoring any new markers.
    
    Fix: record the specific tmp file names left by the interrupted transfer,
    then poll for those specific files to disappear (15 s timeout) instead of
    asserting immediately against all tmp_snapshot_* objects.  New transient
    markers from background snapshot flushes are correctly ignored.

    temporarily produce fresh tmp_ markers during serializeSnapshotToDisk.
    The immediate assertion catches these transient markers as false positives.
    
    The local_disk variant was never flaky because it checks the specific
    tmp file path from the interrupted transfer, ignoring any new markers.
    
    Fix: record the specific tmp file names left by the interrupted transfer,
    then poll for those specific files to disappear (15 s timeout) instead of
    asserting immediately against all tmp_snapshot_* objects.  New transient
    markers from background snapshot flushes are correctly ignored.

## What the task's change actually is

The two bullet points describe edits entirely within `tests/integration/test_keeper_snapshot_chunked_transfer/test.py`:

- Line 218: `interrupted_tmp_names = {o.object_name for o in tmp_objects}` → a set of `(o.object_name, o.last_modified)` tuples.
- Line 244: `if o.object_name in interrupted_tmp_names` → match against the `(object_name, last_modified)` tuple.

`last_modified` is S3 object metadata returned by `minio_client.list_objects` — a purely test-side concept with no counterpart in the C++ source. This is a **test-hardening change**, following directly from the prior commit `7880ce7fb` ("Fix flaky ... by narrowing S3 tmp assertion"). Its purpose is to stop counting a *newly re-received* `tmp_snapshot_<idx>.bin` object (same name, because the re-transfer reuses the same log index after restart) as if it were the original interrupted one.

## The source feature it verifies already exists

The behavior under test — "a node cleans up incomplete snapshot transfers to remote object storage after restarting" — is already implemented in `src/Coordination/KeeperSnapshotManager.cpp:694-748`, in the `KeeperSnapshotManager` constructor's `load_snapshot_from_disk`:

- It scans each snapshot disk, including the S3 `snapshot_storage_disk` (`keeper_snap_s3`, an `s3_plain` disk per the remote config in `keeper_snapshot_utils.py:19-34`).
- It collects `tmp_`-prefixed markers into `incomplete_files`, pairs them with any partial `snapshot_` object (removing both via `clean_incomplete_file`), and unconditionally removes any leftover `tmp_` marker in the final loop (`KeeperSnapshotManager.cpp:747-748`).

So the interrupted `tmp_snapshot_<idx>.bin` marker created by `beginSnapshotReceiveToDisk` (`:822`) is removed on restart on the remote path. The committed name-based polling test passing on master already confirms this cleanup works for `s3_plain`.

## Why no source change is warranted

The tuple form is strictly *more lenient* than the name form — it only stops counting a coincidentally same-named new object, i.e. it removes a false-positive. It cannot require any additional source functionality; if anything it makes an otherwise-flaky test pass reliably against the existing, already-correct cleanup.
